title: A Noetherian local Nagata domain has reduced completion
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] which is a Nagata ring [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring]. Then its $\mathfrak m$-adic completion $\varprojlim_n A/\mathfrak m^n$ is reduced; equivalently $A$ is analytically unramified [def-weil-pbc-analytically-unramified].

proof.text: Prove by natural-number induction that every Noetherian local Nagata domain of Krull dimension at most n is analytically unramified. The bound ringKrullDim_le_spanFinrank_maximalIdeal supplies such an n for the original ring. At n = 0, Ring.KrullDimLE.isField_of_isDomain gives a field; its maximal ideal is zero and AdicCompletion.ofAlgEquiv identifies its completion with itself. This also handles fields in any positive-dimensional induction step.

Construct S as integralClosure A (FractionRing A). Apply the Nagata-domain N-2 theorem and isN1_of_isN2 to obtain Module.Finite A S. Mathlib gives Noetherianity and integrality from finiteness, and integralClosure.isIntegrallyClosedOfFiniteExtension gives normality. Finite-over-Nagata gives IsNagataRing S. Integral extension dimension bounds dim S by dim A.

For each prime p of S over the maximal ideal of A, S_p is a Noetherian local normal domain and is Nagata. Its dimension is the height of p, which is at most dim S, hence at most the induction bound for A. Thus the assertion for normal local Nagata domains at that same bound will give reduced completions for every factor.

Use completion_finite_extension_decomposition at the maximal ideal m of A to identify C tensor_A S with the product of those reduced local completions, where C is the completion of A_m. C is flat over A_m by Mathlib completion flatness, and over A by flat localization and Module.Flat.trans. The inclusion A into S is injective. Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft_injective therefore embeds C into C tensor_A S; isReduced_of_injective descends reducedness from the product to C. IsLocalization.atUnits identifies A with A_m, and AdicCompletion.exists_ringEquiv identifies their maximal-ideal completions. Descend reducedness along this equivalence to obtain analytic unramifiedness of A.

It remains to establish the normal local assertion at bound n+1 using the induction hypothesis at n. If the normal ring is a field, use the zero-ideal completion argument. Otherwise choose nonzero x in its maximal ideal. The principal-quotient associated-height theorem gives height one for every associated prime p of R/(x). Each contains (x), since the annihilator of R/(x) is (x). A prime q between (x) and p cannot be zero. A strict containment q < p would force height(q)+1 <= height(p)=1, contradicting height(q)>=1. Thus p is minimal over (x). Localization normality and the equality dim R_p = height(p) = 1 give regularity by the one-dimensional regularity/normality equivalence.

For such an associated prime p, the element x is a nonzero divisor in the domain R and maps to zero in R/p. Mathlib ringKrullDim_succ_le_of_surjective gives dim(R/p)+1 <= dim R <= n+1. Cancel one using ENat.WithBot.add_le_add_one_right_iff to obtain dim(R/p)<=n. The quotient is a Noetherian local domain and is Nagata by finite-over-Nagata. Apply the induction hypothesis. The image of the original maximal ideal is the quotient maximal ideal by IsLocalRing.map_maximalIdeal_of_surjective, so this proves Ideal.IsAnalyticallyUnramified p with exactly its defined ideal. Apply the principal-quotient criterion to x and the minimality, regularity and analytic-unramifiedness just proved. This completes the normal step, normalization descent, and induction.
